caption: Brendan Ngwa Nforbi v. Home Depot U.S.A., Inc.
court: USDC E.D. Cal. — Sacramento Division (proposed direct filing)
status: FEDERAL REDRAFT — E.D. Cal. Sacramento complaint now pleads § 1331 plus alternative § 1332; warehouse/fulfillment (not DOT); CSC service; and § 290.46 source/use as I&B ultimate facts. Inspection demands are drafted but unsigned/unserved. Discovery date remains the filing gate.
note: The September 8, 2026 San Joaquin packet is historical work product only; it never reached the clerk. Generate the federal review-draft PDF with internal/scripts/matter37-edca-complaint.py. Unsigned inspection demands: internal/docs/matter-37/INSPECTION_DEMAND_FIRST_ADVANTAGE.md and PERSONNEL_FILE_DEMAND_HOME_DEPOT.md. Do not treat another employer's report as Home Depot's report. Do not invent a FCRA/ICRAA discovery date. Serve CSC, not 5395 Hopkins Road.
defendants: Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. is the proposed sole opening defendant as employer/user of the report. First Advantage Background Services Corp. is pleaded as Home Depot's CRA on information and belief based on Home Depot-branded federal-court exhibits, separate federal litigation, and First Advantage public screening materials; it remains a nonparty discovery source unless Home Depot-specific records support an independent CRA claim.
causes: [FEDERAL ANCHOR] FCRA, 15 U.S.C. § 1681b(b)(3)(A) — Home Depot allegedly took adverse employment action based in whole or in part on the First Advantage report without first providing the report and written Summary of Rights; negligent/willful remedies under §§ 1681o/1681n.

[DISTINCT STATE OMISSION] ICRAA, Civ. Code §§ 1786.40 and 1786.50 — upon denying/ending employment under circumstances in which an investigative report was obtained, Home Depot allegedly failed to advise Plaintiff and supply the CRA name/address. Pleaded as a different omission from the FCRA pre-adverse failure to avoid § 1786.52(a) same-act duplication.

[I&B ULTIMATE FACTS] Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E), (j)(4)(A) — complaint pleads on information and belief that First Advantage furnished Plaintiff's California-registry information and Home Depot used it for the Tracy employment decision, supported by same-consumer UPS/FedEx comparators. Exact source-field wording remains reserved for discovery. A Home Depot-specific report would convert this from I&B to documentary fact.
[OMITTED] UCL — limited remedial upside and unnecessary federal standing/remedy side fight.
[OMITTED] CCRAA — reserve unless the actual Home Depot product is an ordinary consumer credit report rather than an investigative employment report.
[OMITTED] Tameny / IIED — approximate August 2024 adverse-action date creates facial two-year limitations problems.
[RESERVED] FCRA § 1681b(b)(2)(A), Fair Chance Act / FEHA, and First Advantage vendor claims — add only if the actual forms, exhaustion record, or CRA conduct support them.
key_facts: Home Depot accepted Plaintiff for warehouse / distribution / fulfillment work at 5395 Hopkins Road, Tracy, began onboarding, ran an employment background check, and then stopped the employment. The Tracy site is a DC, not a DOT driving assignment. Public records support First Advantage as Home Depot's CRA. The complaint alleges as ultimate facts on I&B that First Advantage furnished Home Depot Plaintiff's § 290.46 information and Home Depot used it. Factual basis includes Plaintiff's contemporaneous California registry listing, UPS's First Advantage report on the same Plaintiff showing California-registry sourcing as the adverse/decisional component, FedEx's admission that its First Advantage report identified Plaintiff as a California registrant, and Home Depot's cessation of onboarding after the screen.
procedural_status: Pre-filing federal redraft on branch matter37-edca-federal-redraft-v2 / draft PR #795. Prior signed San Joaquin complaint dated September 8, 2026 was never filed. Proposed forum is E.D. Cal. Sacramento on FCRA § 1331 plus supplemental California claims, with diversity § 1332 pleaded in the alternative (Delaware / Atlanta PPB / California plaintiff; AIC aggregated without inventing a wage rate). Serve CSC at 2710 Gateway Oaks Drive, Suite 150N, Sacramento. Unsigned §§ 1786.22 / 1198.5 demands are drafted. Filing gates: true discovery date (do not use August 2024), Plaintiff signature, official JS-44 / AO-440, and a final hostile audit of every I&B allegation.
damages: Federal draft seeks nonduplicative actual/compensatory damages including lost employment compensation; FCRA remedies under §§ 1681n/1681o; ICRAA actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater, plus punitive damages if the statutory showing is met; and remedies authorized by Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A). No wage rate or duration is presently fixed in the record. Diversity AIC is pleaded in the aggregate without a made-up hourly rate.
risk: Primary filing risk remains limitations: if August 2024 were discovery, a September 2026 filing would already be late. Plead 2024 as discovery of the employment result only, and fill the true FCRA/ICRAA date before filing. Merits pleading is stronger: First Advantage vendor identity is supported by public Home Depot records; § 290.46 source/use are I&B ultimate facts with UPS/FedEx same-consumer comparator support; chronology no longer states registry reporting as known fact. Exact source wording, adjudication codes, access logs, and reason codes are reserved for discovery.
evidence: Plaintiff's statement — accepted Home Depot Tracy hire/onboarding; employment background check; employment then stopped

Ford v. Home Depot U.S.A., Inc., S.D. Cal. 3:19-cv-00754, Dkt. 1 Ex. 1 — Home Depot-branded California disclosure identifies First Advantage as the CRA Home Depot will use and states pre-adverse report/Summary-of-Rights process
Bolton v. First Advantage LNS Screening Solutions, Inc., S.D.N.Y. 1:14-cv-05735, July 1, 2015 opinion — recounts First Advantage report furnished to prospective employer Home Depot
First Advantage Dec. 4, 2019 workforce-screening announcement featuring a Home Depot representative

Harris v. Home Depot U.S.A., Inc., 114 F. Supp. 3d 868 (N.D. Cal. 2015) — FCRA employment-screening litigation against Home Depot; willfulness/sophistication color only; not a § 1681b(b)(2)(A) count in this complaint
Later publicly indexed THD / First Advantage reports and applicant accounts — corroborative continuity evidence only; not primary pleading proof
Home Depot-specific First Advantage report/order/access/adjudication file — target discovery; exact contents and source fields not yet known
